en: to dazzle; to blind with light; to bedazzle, to delude
usage: Literary verb (letterario) for a light so strong it blinds, and figuratively for dazzling someone into losing judgement; 'abbagliare' is the neutral everyday equivalent, 'abbacinare' is rarer and more vivid, recalling the medieval punishment of blinding with a red-hot basin. Regular -are verb; the past participle 'abbacinato' is also used adjectivally.

examples.it: Il sole di mezzogiorno abbacinava i viandanti sulla strada polverosa.
examples.en: The midday sun dazzled the wayfarers on the dusty road.

examples.it: Abbacinati dalle promesse del demagogo, gli elettori non videro il pericolo.
examples.en: Dazzled by the demagogue's promises, the voters did not see the danger.

examples.it: Temo che tanta ricchezza improvvisa lo abbia abbacinato.
examples.en: I fear that so much sudden wealth has dazzled him.

en: to botch; to do hastily and badly
usage: Colloquial-literary and mildly spregiativo: to throw something together carelessly, especially written work or a repair; stronger and more picturesque than 'raffazzonare' or 'fare alla meglio'. Regular -are verb; the participle 'abborracciato' is common as an adjective ('un discorso abborracciato').

examples.it: Ha abborracciato la relazione in mezz'ora e si vede.
examples.en: He botched the report in half an hour and it shows.

examples.it: Non abborracciare la traduzione: il cliente se ne accorgerebbe subito.
examples.en: Don't botch the translation: the client would notice immediately.

examples.it: Abborracciando la tesi all'ultimo momento, rischiò di essere bocciato.
examples.en: Cobbling together his thesis at the last moment, he risked failing.

en: to beg (for alms); to scrounge, to cadge
usage: Old-fashioned and literary for begging alms; today it survives mainly in 'accattonaggio' (begging) and in the ironic figurative sense of scrounging favours or ideas ('accattare voti, consensi'). Regular -are verb; in Tuscany and the South it can also mean simply to buy or get hold of.

examples.it: Il vecchio accattava il pane di porta in porta.
examples.en: The old man begged for bread from door to door.

examples.it: Non voglio accattare favori da chi mi ha già tradito.
examples.en: I don't want to cadge favours from someone who has already betrayed me.

examples.it: Che il romanziere abbia accattato la trama da un feuilleton è evidente.
examples.en: That the novelist scrounged the plot from a serial is obvious.

en: to grieve; to distress deeply; (accorarsi) to be heartbroken
usage: Literary and affective: to strike someone in the heart with sorrow, deeper and more intimate than 'addolorare' or 'rattristare'. Often found as the pronominal 'accorarsi' (auxiliary essere) and in the participle-adjective 'accorato' ('un appello accorato', a heartfelt plea). Regular -are verb.

examples.it: La notizia della sua partenza mi accorò più di quanto volessi ammettere.
examples.en: The news of his departure grieved me more than I wanted to admit.

examples.it: Non accorarti per cose che non puoi cambiare.
examples.en: Don't grieve over things you cannot change.

examples.it: Ci saremmo accorati inutilmente, se avessimo creduto a quelle voci.
examples.en: We would have grieved needlessly, had we believed those rumours.

en: to apply to (a court); to have recourse to; to take up (an inheritance)
usage: Strictly juridical (giuridico): 'adire il tribunale', 'adire le vie legali' (to take legal action), 'adire un'eredità' (to accept an inheritance). Conjugated with -isc- (adisco) but used almost only in the infinitive, the passato remoto and the participle 'adito'; a solemn Latinism never used in everyday speech, where one says 'rivolgersi al giudice' or 'fare causa'.

examples.it: Se non ci pagheranno entro trenta giorni, adiremo le vie legali.
examples.en: If they don't pay us within thirty days, we will take legal action.

examples.it: Gli eredi hanno adito l'eredità con beneficio d'inventario.
examples.en: The heirs accepted the inheritance with benefit of inventory.

examples.it: Il ricorrente adì la Corte costituzionale lamentando la violazione dell'articolo 3.
examples.en: The appellant applied to the Constitutional Court complaining of a violation of Article 3.

en: to take offence; to become suspicious or resentful; (of a horse) to shy
usage: Literally said of a horse that shies at a shadow; figuratively of a person who takes umbrage at a slight, quieter and more inward than 'offendersi' or 'risentirsi'. The transitive 'adombrare' means to hint at or foreshadow ('adombrare un'ipotesi'). Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Si adombra per un nonnulla, quindi scegli bene le parole.
examples.en: He takes offence at the slightest thing, so choose your words carefully.

examples.it: Il cavallo si adombrò al rumore improvviso e disarcionò il cavaliere.
examples.en: The horse shied at the sudden noise and threw its rider.

examples.it: Temevo che si fosse adombrata per la mia battuta, invece rise.
examples.en: I feared she had taken offence at my joke, but instead she laughed.

en: to free, to emancipate; to redeem (a debt, a property); to stamp (a letter)
usage: Learned verb with two lives: the historical-juridical sense of freeing a slave or redeeming a property from a lien, and the postal sense of putting a stamp on mail ('affrancatura'). The pronominal 'affrancarsi da' (to free oneself from) is the most common modern use, more elevated than 'liberarsi'. Regular -are verb with the -chi/-che spelling change.

examples.it: Solo con lo studio si affrancò dalla miseria in cui era nato.
examples.en: Only through study did he free himself from the poverty into which he was born.

examples.it: La lettera non era stata affrancata a sufficienza ed è tornata indietro.
examples.en: The letter had not been stamped sufficiently and came back.

examples.it: Bisogna che il paese si affranchi dalla dipendenza energetica.
examples.en: The country needs to free itself from energy dependence.

en: to set (a dog) on; to incite, to stir up (against)
usage: Originally said of setting dogs on someone; figuratively, of whipping up a crowd against a target, with a strong spregiativo colouring. Compared with 'istigare' (neutral-juridical) and 'sobillare' (secretly), 'aizzare' suggests open, animal-like provocation. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Il guardiano aizzò i cani contro gli intrusi.
examples.en: The watchman set the dogs on the intruders.

examples.it: Quei giornali hanno aizzato l'opinione pubblica contro i migranti.
examples.en: Those newspapers stirred up public opinion against migrants.

examples.it: Non aizzare i tuoi figli l'uno contro l'altro.
examples.en: Don't set your children against one another.

en: to alienate; to transfer (property); (alienarsi) to lose (sympathy), to become estranged
usage: In legal language it means to transfer ownership ('alienare un immobile'); in philosophical-sociological prose it means to estrange from oneself or from others. The idiom 'alienarsi le simpatie di qualcuno' (to lose someone's goodwill) takes a direct object. Regular -are verb; the adjective 'alienato' also means insane in older usage.

examples.it: Il comune ha alienato diversi immobili per ripianare il bilancio.
examples.en: The municipality sold off several properties to balance the budget.

examples.it: Con quella decisione il ministro si è alienato l'appoggio dei sindacati.
examples.en: With that decision the minister lost the unions' support.

examples.it: Marx sosteneva che il lavoro in fabbrica alienasse l'operaio dal prodotto del suo lavoro.
examples.en: Marx argued that factory work alienated the worker from the product of his labour.

en: to tame; to placate, to soothe (an angry person)
usage: From 'manso' (tame): literally to tame an animal, figuratively to calm an angry person, often with a touch of irony ('lo ammansì con una promessa'). Conjugated with -isc- (ammansisco); the intransitive and pronominal use ('ammansirsi', to calm down) takes essere. Compare 'placare' (neutral) and 'rabbonire' (more colloquial).

examples.it: Il domatore ammansiva le belve con una pazienza infinita.
examples.en: The tamer would tame the beasts with infinite patience.

examples.it: Ci vollero ore prima che il padre si ammansisse.
examples.en: It took hours before the father calmed down.

examples.it: Spero di averlo ammansito con quelle scuse.
examples.en: I hope I have placated him with that apology.

en: to pile up untidily; to heap together
usage: Diminutive-frequentative of 'ammucchiare': to make small, disorderly heaps, with a familiar or faintly scherzoso tone; 'accatastare' implies orderly stacking, 'ammucchiare' is neutral. Regular -are verb; commonly pronominal ('ammonticchiarsi', auxiliary essere).

examples.it: Sulla scrivania si ammonticchiavano lettere mai aperte.
examples.en: Unopened letters were piling up on the desk.

examples.it: Ammonticchiò i vestiti su una sedia e si buttò sul letto.
examples.en: He heaped his clothes on a chair and threw himself on the bed.

examples.it: Se continui ad ammonticchiare scatole in corridoio, non passeremo più.
examples.en: If you keep piling boxes up in the hallway, we won't be able to get through any more.

en: to oppress; to harass; to tyrannise
usage: Learned verb from 'angheria' (abuse of power): to torment someone with repeated exactions and vexations. Close to 'vessare' and 'tiranneggiare', it stresses the arbitrary abuse by a stronger party (a landlord, a boss, an occupier). Regular -are verb: 'angario, angarii'.

examples.it: I contadini erano angariati da un fattore avido e crudele.
examples.en: The peasants were oppressed by a greedy and cruel bailiff.

examples.it: Non permetteremo che un capo angari i dipendenti impunemente.
examples.en: We won't allow a boss to harass employees with impunity.

examples.it: Angariò per anni la moglie, finché lei non trovò il coraggio di andarsene.
examples.en: He tyrannised his wife for years, until she found the courage to leave.

en: to yearn for, to long for; (literary) to pant
usage: Aulic, poetic verb: literally to breathe with difficulty, hence to long ardently for something ('anelare alla libertà'). It governs 'a' and belongs to literary and rhetorical prose; 'desiderare ardentemente' is the neutral equivalent. Regular -are verb: 'anelo' (stress on the first e).

examples.it: Il popolo anelava alla pace dopo dieci anni di guerra.
examples.en: The people yearned for peace after ten years of war.

examples.it: Anelò per tutta la vita a un riconoscimento che non arrivò mai.
examples.en: He longed all his life for a recognition that never came.

examples.it: Chi non anelerebbe a una vita più semplice?
examples.en: Who wouldn't long for a simpler life?

en: to flounder, to flail about; to grope, to fumble
usage: Vivid verb for the disordered movement of the arms in water, in the dark or, figuratively, in a difficult situation ('annaspare tra i debiti', 'annaspare nelle risposte'). Journalistic and literary alike; 'brancolare' implies searching for a way, 'annaspare' helpless agitation. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Il bambino annaspava nell'acqua alta gridando aiuto.
examples.en: The child was floundering in the deep water, shouting for help.

examples.it: L'imputato annaspò per qualche secondo, poi cambiò versione.
examples.en: The defendant floundered for a few seconds, then changed his story.

examples.it: Stanno annaspando da mesi: la società fallirà entro l'anno.
examples.en: They have been floundering for months: the company will go bankrupt within the year.

en: to annihilate; to crush, to reduce to nothing; (annichilirsi) to be overwhelmed
usage: Learned Latinism (from 'nihil'): to reduce to nothing, physically or morally ('una critica che annichilisce'). Rarer than 'annientare' and more often used of psychological crushing; the variant 'annichilare' exists but is rarer. Conjugated with -isc- (annichilisco); the pronominal 'annichilirsi' takes essere.

examples.it: Quel silenzio annichiliva ogni sua velleità di protesta.
examples.en: That silence annihilated any inclination he had to protest.

examples.it: Ci sentimmo annichiliti dalla vastità del deserto.
examples.en: We felt annihilated by the vastness of the desert.

examples.it: Non credo che una sconfitta possa annichilire un partito con tanta storia.
examples.en: I don't think one defeat can annihilate a party with such a long history.

en: to reveal, to make manifest; (appalesarsi) to become evident, to prove to be
usage: Bureaucratic-forensic doublet of 'palesare', typical of court rulings and formal reports ('la censura si appalesa infondata', the objection proves groundless). Almost always pronominal (auxiliary essere) and impersonal; in ordinary prose 'rivelarsi' or 'risultare' are preferable. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Il motivo di ricorso si appalesa manifestamente infondato.
examples.en: The ground of appeal proves manifestly unfounded.

examples.it: Col tempo si appalesarono le vere intenzioni del socio.
examples.en: In time the partner's true intentions became evident.

examples.it: Temo che la sua incompetenza si appaleserà alla prima difficoltà.
examples.en: I fear that his incompetence will become evident at the first difficulty.

en: to ascertain; to verify; to establish (the facts)
usage: Formal-journalistic verb for establishing the truth of something after inquiry ('è stato appurato che'), typical of police reports, investigations and news items. Stronger than 'verificare' (to check): it implies that the doubt has been settled. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Gli inquirenti hanno appurato che l'incendio era doloso.
examples.en: The investigators established that the fire was arson.

examples.it: Prima di accusare qualcuno, bisogna appurare come siano andate le cose.
examples.en: Before accusing anyone, one must ascertain how things went.

examples.it: Una volta appurata la verità, il direttore chiese scusa pubblicamente.
examples.en: Once the truth had been ascertained, the director apologised publicly.

en: to rack one's brains; to fret, to torment oneself
usage: Expressive verb for fruitless mental effort or anxious brooding: 'arrovellarsi il cervello' (to rack one's brains), 'arrovellarsi su un problema'. More agitated than 'scervellarsi', it can also convey anger and frustration. Regular -are verb, always pronominal.

examples.it: Mi arrovello da giorni su come dirglielo.
examples.en: I've been racking my brains for days over how to tell him.

examples.it: Si arrovellò tutta la notte senza trovare una soluzione.
examples.en: He tormented himself all night without finding a solution.

examples.it: È inutile che ti arrovelli: la decisione non dipende da te.
examples.en: There's no point fretting: the decision doesn't depend on you.

en: to indulge in far-fetched reasoning; to concoct convoluted ideas
usage: Scherzoso and slightly spregiativo: to spin over-subtle, tortuous arguments or fanciful theories ('arzigogolare su un testo'). The adjective 'arzigogolato' (convoluted) is more common than the verb itself. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Smettila di arzigogolare e dimmi chiaramente cosa vuoi.
examples.en: Stop going round in circles and tell me clearly what you want.

examples.it: I critici hanno arzigogolato per decenni sul significato di quel verso.
examples.en: Critics have spun elaborate theories for decades about the meaning of that line.

examples.it: Arzigogolando spiegazioni sempre più fantasiose, finì per contraddirsi.
examples.en: Concocting ever more far-fetched explanations, he ended up contradicting himself.

en: to rise (to a higher rank or symbolic status); to attain
usage: Solemn, journalistic-literary verb used almost only in 'assurgere a' (to rise to the status of): 'assurgere a simbolo', 'a emblema', 'a fama nazionale'. Irregular: passato remoto 'assurse', participio 'assurto' (rare); auxiliary essere.

examples.it: Quella foto è assurta a simbolo della resistenza civile.
examples.en: That photograph has become a symbol of civil resistance.

examples.it: Da oscuro funzionario assurse in pochi anni ai vertici del ministero.
examples.en: From an obscure official he rose within a few years to the top of the ministry.

examples.it: Nessuno immaginava che un dialetto potesse assurgere a lingua letteraria.
examples.en: No one imagined that a dialect could rise to the status of a literary language.

en: to draw (water); to draw on, to derive (information, inspiration); to reach
usage: Literally to draw water from a well; figuratively, to draw on a source ('attingere a piene mani da un autore', 'attingere notizie da fonti riservate'). Irregular like 'tingere': passato remoto 'attinsi', participio 'attinto'. In legal Italian it also means to reach or affect someone ('l'accusa attinge anche il sindaco').

examples.it: Le donne attingevano l'acqua alla fontana del villaggio.
examples.en: The women drew water at the village fountain.

examples.it: Il regista ha attinto a piene mani dal cinema muto.
examples.en: The director drew heavily on silent cinema.

examples.it: Da dove avrà attinto informazioni così precise?
examples.en: Where can he have drawn such precise information from?

en: to notice; to become aware of, to realise
usage: Literary counterpart of 'accorgersi', common in classical prose and in the passato remoto ('si avvide che'); the adjective 'avveduto' (shrewd) and the noun 'avvedutezza' are more frequent than the verb today. Irregular like 'vedere': 'mi avvedo, mi avvidi, avveduto (or avvisto), mi avvedrò'.

examples.it: Si avvide troppo tardi dell'inganno.
examples.en: He realised the deception too late.

examples.it: Non ci si avvede del tempo che passa finché non è passato.
examples.en: One does not notice time passing until it has passed.

examples.it: Temo che se ne siano avveduti tutti tranne lui.
examples.en: I fear everyone noticed except him.

en: to accustom; (avvezzarsi) to get used to
usage: Slightly old-fashioned, literary or regional (Tuscan) synonym of 'abituare'; the participle 'avvezzo' ('non sono avvezzo a simili trattamenti', I'm not used to such treatment) is the form most alive in cultivated speech. Regular -are verb; the pronominal 'avvezzarsi' takes essere.

examples.it: La nonna ci aveva avvezzati a non sprecare nulla.
examples.en: Grandmother had accustomed us to waste nothing.

examples.it: Non è avvezzo a ricevere rifiuti, e reagì male.
examples.en: He is not used to being refused, and he reacted badly.

examples.it: Col tempo ti avvezzerai al clima di questa città.
examples.en: In time you'll get used to this city's climate.

en: to clasp tightly; to grip; (avvinghiarsi) to cling to
usage: To hold with a tight, almost snake-like grip (from 'vinco', willow twig); stronger and more physical than 'abbracciare' or 'stringere', frequent in narrative prose. Commonly pronominal: 'avvinghiarsi a qualcuno' (to cling to someone, auxiliary essere). Regular -are verb.

examples.it: La bambina si avvinghiò alle gambe della madre.
examples.en: The little girl clung to her mother's legs.

examples.it: L'edera aveva avvinghiato tutto il tronco.
examples.en: The ivy had wrapped itself around the whole trunk.

examples.it: I due lottatori si erano avvinghiati in una presa senza via d'uscita.
examples.en: The two wrestlers had locked each other in a hold with no way out.

en: to delight in, to bask in; to revel in
usage: Literary and often ironic: to take blissful, self-satisfied pleasure in something ('bearsi del proprio successo'). Compare 'compiacersi' (self-satisfaction), 'crogiolarsi' (to wallow comfortably) and 'godere' (neutral). Regular -are verb: 'mi beo, ti bei, si bea'.

examples.it: Si beava degli applausi come un attore alla prima.
examples.en: He basked in the applause like an actor on opening night.

examples.it: Ci bearemo di questo silenzio finché durerà.
examples.en: We will revel in this silence for as long as it lasts.

examples.it: Non voglio che ti bei di un successo che non è tuo.
examples.en: I don't want you to delight in a success that isn't yours.

en: to mock; to fool, to outwit; (beffarsi di) to scoff at
usage: From 'beffa' (a practical joke or humiliating trick): to mock someone or, especially, to outwit them ('la squadra è stata beffata allo scadere', beaten by a last-second goal). The pronominal 'beffarsi di' (auxiliary essere) means to scoff at or defy ('beffarsi della legge'). Regular -are verb; journalistic in sports and politics.

examples.it: I ladri hanno beffato la sorveglianza entrando dal tetto.
examples.en: The thieves outwitted the security guards by getting in through the roof.

examples.it: Si beffava delle nostre paure con un sorriso di superiorità.
examples.en: He scoffed at our fears with a superior smile.

examples.it: Chi crede di poter beffare il fisco per sempre si illude.
examples.en: Anyone who thinks they can fool the tax authorities forever is deluding themselves.

en: to mumble; to chew laboriously, to mouth (words)
usage: Onomatopoeic and spregiativo: to chew slowly with the mouth half open, hence to mutter words indistinctly ('biascicare una preghiera', 'biascicare due parole'). 'Farfugliare' is confused mumbling, 'borbottare' grumbling, 'biascicare' sluggish and toothless. Regular -are verb (biascichi, biascichiamo).

examples.it: Il vecchio biascicava una preghiera davanti all'altare.
examples.en: The old man was mumbling a prayer in front of the altar.

examples.it: Biascicò qualche scusa e se ne andò.
examples.en: He mumbled some excuse and left.

examples.it: Non biascicare: parla chiaro, che non ti capisco.
examples.en: Don't mumble: speak clearly, I can't understand you.

en: to blather; to prattle, to talk nonsense
usage: Spregiativo verb for loud, empty, endless talk; alongside 'cianciare' (idle chatter) and 'straparlare' (talking wildly), it stresses noise and pomposity, like a demagogue on a podium. Regular -are verb ('blàtero', stress on the first a).

examples.it: Blaterava di complotti senza uno straccio di prova.
examples.en: He was blathering about conspiracies without a shred of proof.

examples.it: Cosa avrà blaterato per due ore in quella riunione?
examples.en: What can he have been prattling on about for two hours in that meeting?

examples.it: Lasciate che blateri: nessuno lo ascolta più.
examples.en: Let him blather: nobody listens to him any more.

en: to brandish; to wield
usage: To raise and shake a weapon threateningly ('brandire una spada, un bastone'), and figuratively any object used as a weapon ('brandire la Costituzione contro gli avversari'). Literary and journalistic; conjugated with -isc- (brandisco). 'Impugnare' just means to grip, while 'brandire' implies the threatening flourish.

examples.it: Il cavaliere brandì la spada e si lanciò nella mischia.
examples.en: The knight brandished his sword and threw himself into the fray.

examples.it: I manifestanti brandivano cartelli e bandiere.
examples.en: The demonstrators were waving placards and flags.

examples.it: Non brandire il regolamento come una clava ogni volta che qualcuno dissente.
examples.en: Don't wield the rulebook like a club every time someone disagrees.

en: to swarm; to teem (with)
usage: Said of insects or crowds moving in confused masses, and of places teeming with them ('la piazza brulicava di turisti'). Common in descriptive prose and reportage; 'pullulare' is the near synonym for things springing up everywhere, 'formicolare' stresses ant-like movement. Regular -are verb (brulichi).

examples.it: Il mercato brulicava di gente fin dalle prime ore del mattino.
examples.en: The market was swarming with people from the early hours of the morning.

examples.it: Sotto la pietra brulicavano centinaia di formiche.
examples.en: Hundreds of ants were swarming under the stone.

examples.it: Temo che d'estate la spiaggia brulichi di bagnanti.
examples.en: I fear that in summer the beach will be teeming with bathers.

en: to slander; to defame falsely
usage: To make false accusations against someone knowingly; in Italian criminal law 'calunnia' is specifically the offence of falsely accusing someone of a crime before the authorities, distinct from 'diffamazione'. 'Diffamare' is the broader term, 'denigrare' need not involve falsehood. Regular -are verb ('calunnio, calunni').

examples.it: Lo hanno calunniato per anni sui giornali di partito.
examples.en: They slandered him for years in the party newspapers.

examples.it: Chi calunnia un innocente davanti al giudice commette reato.
examples.en: Whoever falsely accuses an innocent person before a judge commits a crime.

examples.it: Se mi calunniassero in quel modo, li querelerei.
examples.en: If they slandered me like that, I would sue them.

en: to extract (a secret, a promise) by cunning; to snatch, to seize
patterns: carpire la buona fede di qualcuno
usage: To obtain something by deceit, flattery or force: 'carpire un segreto', 'carpire la buona fede di qualcuno' (to abuse someone's good faith), 'carpire il consenso'. Conjugated with -isc- (carpisco); it always suggests underhandedness, unlike 'ottenere' or 'strappare' (to wring out openly).

examples.it: Con domande apparentemente innocenti gli carpì tutti i dettagli del piano.
examples.en: With seemingly innocent questions she extracted from him every detail of the plan.

examples.it: I truffatori carpiscono la fiducia degli anziani fingendosi tecnici del gas.
examples.en: The swindlers gain the trust of the elderly by pretending to be gas technicians.

examples.it: Temo che gli abbiano carpito la firma con l'inganno.
examples.en: I fear they obtained his signature by deceit.

en: to conceal, to hide (literary)
usage: Literary and elevated equivalent of 'nascondere', very common in journalism in the pronominal 'celarsi dietro' ('dietro l'offerta si cela una truffa', auxiliary essere) and in the participle 'celato'. Use it for secrets, intentions and feelings rather than physical objects. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Celò a tutti la malattia fino all'ultimo.
examples.en: He concealed his illness from everyone until the end.

examples.it: Dietro quella cortesia si cela un calcolo preciso.
examples.en: Behind that courtesy lies a precise calculation.

examples.it: Non credo che ci abbia celato nulla di importante.
examples.en: I don't think he has hidden anything important from us.

en: to chatter idly; to prattle, to talk nonsense
usage: Spregiativo and somewhat literary (Manzoni and Verga use it): to talk without substance, to gossip. Compared with 'chiacchierare' (neutral) it always implies emptiness; 'blaterare' adds noise and pomposity. Regular -are verb: 'ciancio, ciancia', with the i dropped before e/i ('cianci', 'ciancerò').

examples.it: Ciancia di politica senza aver mai letto un giornale.
examples.en: He prattles about politics without ever having read a newspaper.

examples.it: Cianciarono per ore davanti al bar, e nessuno concluse nulla.
examples.en: They chattered for hours outside the café, and nobody got anything done.

examples.it: Non è tempo di cianciare: bisogna agire.
examples.en: This is no time for idle talk: we must act.

en: to dawdle, to fiddle about; to cut or crease (fabric) clumsily
usage: Familiar, faintly scherzoso verb from tailoring (to cut cloth badly, to crease it): today mostly to fiddle aimlessly or waste time on small useless actions ('cincischiare con il telefono'). 'Gingillarsi' is the closest synonym; 'indugiare' is more literary. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Ha cincischiato tutto il pomeriggio senza scrivere una riga.
examples.en: He dawdled all afternoon without writing a line.

examples.it: Smettila di cincischiare quella tovaglia e ascoltami.
examples.en: Stop fiddling with that tablecloth and listen to me.

examples.it: Se continuerai a cincischiare, perderemo il treno.
examples.en: If you keep dawdling, we'll miss the train.

en: to coerce; to constrain (someone's will)
usage: Juridical Latinism: to force someone's will by violence or threat ('coartare la libertà di scelta'), the technical noun being 'coartazione'. In ordinary prose 'costringere' or 'forzare' are used; 'coartare' appears in rulings, contracts and philosophical texts. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Il contratto è nullo se la volontà del contraente è stata coartata.
examples.en: The contract is void if the contracting party's will was coerced.

examples.it: Nessuno può essere coartato a testimoniare contro un familiare.
examples.en: No one can be coerced into testifying against a family member.

examples.it: Sostenne che le pressioni della famiglia avessero coartato la sua scelta.
examples.en: He argued that family pressure had constrained his choice.

en: to insulate (thermally or acoustically)
usage: Technical term of building and engineering: to fit walls, roofs or pipes with insulating material ('coibente'), the noun being 'coibentazione'. Everyday speech says 'isolare', but the technical verb is standard in renovation talk and energy-efficiency regulations. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Abbiamo coibentato il tetto per ridurre le spese di riscaldamento.
examples.en: We insulated the roof to cut heating costs.

examples.it: Se coibentassero le pareti, la casa passerebbe in classe energetica B.
examples.en: If they insulated the walls, the house would move up to energy class B.

examples.it: Le tubature vanno coibentate prima dell'inverno.
examples.en: The pipes must be insulated before winter.

en: to reconcile, to balance (conflicting interests); to temper
usage: Learned verb of juridical and political prose: to weigh opposing interests so that each is partly satisfied ('contemperare le esigenze della sicurezza con quelle della privacy'). 'Conciliare' is the everyday synonym; 'bilanciare' the economic one. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: La legge cerca di contemperare la libertà di stampa con la tutela della reputazione.
examples.en: The law seeks to balance freedom of the press with the protection of reputation.

examples.it: Non è facile contemperare interessi così divergenti.
examples.en: It is not easy to reconcile such divergent interests.

examples.it: Il giudice contemperò le ragioni delle parti con un compromesso equo.
examples.en: The judge balanced the parties' claims with a fair compromise.

en: to contravene; to infringe, to breach
usage: Juridical-bureaucratic verb governing 'a': 'contravvenire a una norma, a un divieto, agli obblighi'. Irregular like 'venire' (contravvengo, contravvenni, contravvenuto, contravverrò) but, unlike 'venire', it takes avere. Its noun 'contravvenzione' means a minor offence or a fine.

examples.it: Chi contravviene al divieto di sosta rischia la rimozione del veicolo.
examples.en: Whoever breaches the no-parking rule risks having their vehicle towed away.

examples.it: Il soldato contravvenne agli ordini e fu processato.
examples.en: The soldier disobeyed orders and was court-martialled.

examples.it: Hanno contravvenuto a tutte le clausole del contratto.
examples.en: They have breached every clause of the contract.

en: to become vexed; to frown, to be sullen
usage: Literary verb for a mixture of anger and grief that shows on the face ('un volto corrucciato', 'la fronte corrucciata'). The participle-adjective 'corrucciato' is far more common than the finite verb. Regular -are verb (mi corruccio, ti corrucci).

examples.it: Si corrucciò quando seppe che non era stato invitato.
examples.en: He grew sullen when he learned he had not been invited.

examples.it: Perché ti corrucci per una sciocchezza simile?
examples.en: Why are you getting upset about such a trifle?

examples.it: La maestra ci guardò corrucciata e non disse nulla.
examples.en: The teacher looked at us with a frown and said nothing.
